title: Account-triggered Priority Allocator & Sprint Shepherding
creator: Maya Singh
description:
Problem: Senior customer requests and escalation threads currently arrive as freeform asks into the Intake queue; engineering and PM time is spent repeatedly qualifying scope and negotiating delivery windows. This leads to long TTR for top accounts and poor predictability for commercial commitments.

Goal: Build an "account-triggered priority allocator" — a compact decision graph and lightweight contract generator that converts validated top-account signals into an actionable tranche on the roadmap with attached sprint shepherding guidance. The system should: 1) automatically map incoming escalation metadata to a priority bucket, 2) suggest a minimal scoped deliverable and tentative sprint window, and 3) create a follow-up runbook for engineering and Customer Success to align expectations.

Why now: Increasing number of strategic seats with bespoke asks and our push to standardize enterprise SLAs requires a repeatable, auditable intake-to-commit flow. This reduces negotiation overhead and prevents unexpected scope creep during delivery.

Scope:
- In scope: decision-graph rules, contract template (1-pager) generator, integration point with Intake dashboard, small UI in Console for PM/CS to accept suggested tranche, and a sprint shepherding checklist template.
- Out of scope: automated allocation of Dedicated capacity, billing changes, or changes to legal contract language (legal sign-off will be manual).

Stakeholders: PM (Maya Singh), Eng lead (Ethan Park), CS lead (Rosa Alvarez), Legal reviewer (Amir Patel), Design (Priya Rao), Solutions Eng (Connor Mills).

Non-goals: Autonomously committing engineering sprint capacity without explicit PM approval; replacing existing escalation Slack channels (we will link to them).
acceptance_criteria: 1) Decision graph spec reviewed and approved by PM, Eng, CS and Legal. 2) Prototype integration in Intake dashboard that surfaces recommended priority and suggested tranche. 3) 1-pager contract generator produces a filled template based on inputs and can be stored as an artifact link. 4) Sprint shepherding checklist created and available as a checklist template in Confluence. 5) Pilot with 3 top accounts completed, with CS feedback captured and NPS-like signal >= 70.
notes: Trade-offs considered: we could build a fully configurable rules engine (highly flexible) vs. a limited decision graph (faster to deliver). Recommendation: start with a curated decision graph plus a micro-configurable override for PM/CS — iterate to a rules engine if adoption demands it.
Quality gating: suggested tranche must include clear acceptance criteria and an initial risk estimate (low/med/high). Engineering will not accept tranche without those fields.
Data model: Intake form must capture: account_tier, ARR, escalation_type, compliance_required, target_region, and competitive_urgency. These inputs feed the decision graph mapping.
